AI can already cut, caption and format a clip for you. Free GitHub skills teach Claude the editing part in minutes. So why isn't everyone going viral off podcast clips? Because editing was never the hard part. Choosing the moment is. AI does not know which 47 seconds out of a two hour conversation deserve to become the clip. No context. No content intelligence. Here is how you build that layer. Scrape the latest 100 clips from the biggest podcast short form accounts. Steven Bartlett, Chris Williamson, Alex Hormozi, anyone running serious long form volume. Capture views, post date, duration, transcript, text overlay and format. Then scrape their original long form episodes and pull the complete transcripts with timestamps. The timestamps are non negotiable. They are what lets Claude match every clip back to the exact episode and the exact moment it came from. Now you reverse engineer the decision. Why those 47 seconds. Where the clip starts. What context got removed. Whether the payoff moved forward. What spoken hook, text overlay and format they used. And how it performed against that account's normal clips. Run enough of these and the patterns surface. Turn the patterns into a Claude skill that understands how the best podcast teams select and package their clips. Then hand it any new timestamped transcript. It returns the strongest moments, exact timestamps, hook options, text overlays, formats and editing instructions. The editing skill does the easy part. None of this needs new software. The tools exist. The clipping skills exist. The data is public. Nobody is assembling it into an intelligence layer. Impossible to fail does not mean every clip goes viral. It means every clip starts with real evidence, and every result makes the next selection smarter. Build the selection layer first. The edit is the easy bit.

The 4 levels of using AI at work How to use AI at work: there are four levels, and most people never leave level one. Chat. You paste something into ChatGPT or Claude, it answers, you copy it back out. Useful, but you're the delivery guy carrying every answer between your apps by hand. Context. Give it your price list, your process docs and ten emails you wrote so it learns how you sound. Same AI, completely different answers, because now it answers like it works at your company. Connected tools. Out of the box, AI can't open your CRM or read your spreadsheet. Almost every app has a door for other software called an API, and MCP is a standard plug that lets AI walk through those doors. Once it's connected, it sees your contacts, your sheets and your email, and it acts: update, send, create. Updating 2,000 customer records from last month's invoices is two weeks of somebody's life. Connected AI does it in minutes. Run it on ten records first, check them, then let it do the rest. Automations. Level three still needs you to ask. Level four starts on its own: a new lead comes in, an invoice lands, Monday at 8am. A tool like n8n moves the data between your apps, and the AI in the middle does the thinking: reads the email, picks the category, writes the reply. Your business keeps running while you sleep. The whole ladder: chat, context, connected tools, automations. On level three you talk and it does the work. On level four you don't even have to talk. If you want to climb all four, from your first chat to your first AI automation, I built seven courses for exactly that, in order, inside my community. How to build a $25K website with AI, every click from zero (Claude Code + n8n, beginner guide) An agency would charge about twenty-five thousand dollars for this website. Here's how you build it with AI, from zero, every click, and wire it so every good lead gets a real answer in under a minute. You never type code: at every step you say one sentence to Claude, and it does the work. What you need: a paid Claude plan (Pro is enough) and a few free accounts: GitHub, n8n, Resend, Vercel, plus an Anthropic console account with $5 of credit. The Cloudflare tunnel needs no account. The steps, and the exact sentences to say: 1. Download VS Code. Open Extensions, search "Claude Code", click Install, click the spark icon and sign in. Make an empty folder called alder-slate and open it. 2. Say: "Interview me about my business, then write CLAUDE.md." Answer its questions in plain words. CLAUDE.md is the brief Claude reads every time: colors, fonts, services and rules (no stock photos, no purple gradients). 3. Say: "Build the website from CLAUDE.md, with a big serif headline, lots of space, real-looking photos, and a five-step quote form." For a real client, use their real job photos. 4. Say: "Take screenshots of every page on a laptop and a phone, look at them, and fix what's off." 5. The form goes to the website's own server first, which adds a secret password from the .env file (a locked drawer for your keys) before passing the request to n8n. The browser never sees it. 6. Create a free GitHub account. Say: "Put this project on my GitHub." Open the link Claude gives you, type the code, click Continue, then Authorize. 7. Say: "Set up n8n on my computer." Create the owner account, then Settings, n8n API, create an API key and copy it (you only see it once). In the Anthropic console, add $5 of credit and create an API key. 8. Say: "Connect yourself to my n8n, here are the two keys." Claude adds the n8n MCP (a connector that lets Claude work inside n8n). Type /mcp in a new conversation and n8n shows connected. 9. Say: "Add a workflow to CLAUDE.md. When the website sends a new project request, save it to a leads table, check the ZIP code and budget with simple rules, have Claude score it and write a reply, then email Marco and the customer." Then: "Now build that workflow in n8n." 10. Create a free Resend account, API Keys, create, copy. Say: "Use this key to send the emails from n8n." Until you add your own domain, every email comes to you. 11. Say: "Add a daily follow-up, and alert Marco if anything breaks." 12. Say: "Give my n8n webhook a public address with a Cloudflare tunnel, and only let the webhook through." The editor stays closed; the webhook still asks for the password. 13. On Vercel, Continue with GitHub, Add New, Project, Import. Ask Claude: "Which environment variables does Vercel need?" Paste the two (the webhook address and the secret), Deploy. 14. Before real customers: n8n on a real server set to your time zone, your own domain in Vercel and the Pro plan, and verify your domain in Resend. 15. Say: "Install Cloudflare's security audit skill from GitHub." Then: "Security audit this codebase." Then: "Fix what you found." Finally, make fresh keys in every app and swap them in. If you don't even know what I'm talking about and you want to learn all of this from scratch, I break every step down inside my community.
